notes: assoc-ref-missing-key: with_skill 5/5 vs baseline 4/5 — baseline's only miss was asserting the answer in its opening sentence before quoting the transcript; both arms independently verified via a real REPL.

profile-fib22: with_skill 5/5 vs baseline 4/5 — baseline used the programmatic (statprof ...) call instead of the REPL's ,profile meta-command the skill documents; both correctly worked around a too-short workload and landed on the same conclusion.

reload-after-edit: TIE, 4/5 both arms — zero discrimination. A capable baseline agent independently checked the pre-edit value, recognised staleness, and reloaded explicitly without being told to. Both missed the same expectation (noting that $N numbering restarts per connection) — that expectation may be miscalibrated/irrelevant to this prompt and is a candidate for revision.

lint-proxy-script: TIE, 5/5 both arms — zero discrimination. This repo's own Makefile 'lint' target already encodes 'there is no linter, use guild3 compile -W3', so a baseline agent that reads the Makefile gets the same answer as one that reads the skill.

Overall for this iteration: guile-repl-eval's measurable value (given a Sonnet-5-class baseline) is concentrated in write-up discipline (evidence before claims) and knowing the ,profile meta-command surface — not in the reload or lint scenarios, where a capable baseline already lands on the right behavior from the repo's own artifacts.
